**Surah 93, Al-Duha, is Meccan** [[Al-Daylami? No: Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi reported on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "Surah al-Duha was revealed in Makkah." See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/539.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us: Zuhayr related to us: al-Aswad ibn Qays related to us, who said: "I heard Jundub ibn Sufyan say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became ill and did not get up for the night, or for two or three nights. A woman came and said: 'O Muhammad, I hope that your devil has forsaken you. I have not seen him come near you for two or three nights.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you.﴾" [[Related by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah al-Duha, chapter "(Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you)": 8/710, and in other places; and by Muslim in Jihad and Expeditions, chapter "What the Prophet (ﷺ) suffered from the harm of the polytheists and the hypocrites", no. 1997: 3/1422.]]

It is said: the woman who spoke these words was Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab.

The commentators (al-mufassirun) said: The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Dhu al-Qarnayn, the People of the Cave (ashab al-kahf) and the Spirit (al-Ruh). He said: "I will inform you tomorrow," and he did not say "if Allah wills." So revelation was withheld from him... [[These reports cited by the author are mentioned by: al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 15/200-205; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/363-370, 373; al-Qurtubi: 10/358-360; and al-Khazin: 4/160-165.

These reports, in this detail concerning the departure of the youths, their names and the name of their dog, etc., are in their entirety taken from the People of the Book who had embraced Islam (Ahl al-Kitab who converted). Some Companions and Successors (tabi'un) transmitted them from them and related them because of their strangeness and wonder. We set down here some words of the verifying scholars and commentators concerning these reports, which spare us from commenting on the tafsir in many places:

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir (3/76-79): "...Allah the Exalted has not told us the location of this cave, nor in which lands of the earth it lies, since there is no benefit for us in it and no legislative purpose. Some commentators have burdened themselves by mentioning opinions about it... Allah knows best in which of Allah's lands it is. Had there been a religious benefit in it, Allah and His Messenger would have guided us to it... He informed us of its description and did not inform us of its location."

After mentioning some opinions about the dog of the People of the Cave and its color, he said: "They differed about its color in opinions that have no outcome, no benefit, no evidence, and no need for them. Rather, they are among the things forbidden, for their basis is conjecture about the unseen (rajm bil-ghayb)."

And he said about the names of the youths: "...As for naming them with these names and the name of their dog, there is doubt about its authenticity, and Allah knows best, for most of that is taken from the People of the Book. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾, meaning: with ease and gentleness, for knowing that matter yields no great benefit."

He said in al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya (2/115): "...Many storytellers (qussas) and commentators have related for this dog a lengthy account and report, most of it taken from the Israelite narratives (Isra'iliyyat), and much of it false and of no benefit, such as their disagreement over its name and its color."

Ustadh Sayyid Qutb said in his book Fi Zilal al-Qur'an (15/2260-2261): "The story of the People of the Cave comes, presenting a model of faith in believing souls: how they find peace in it, prefer it over the adornment and goods of the earth, and take refuge in the cave when it is hard for them to live among the people; and how Allah watches over these believing souls, protects them from trial, and envelops them with mercy.

In the story there are various narrations and many sayings. They have appeared in some ancient books and legends in various forms. We stop at what has come in the Qur'an, for it is the sole certain source, and we set aside all the other narrations and legends that have crept into the tafsirs without authentic chains, especially since the Noble Qur'an has forbidden seeking rulings from other than the Qur'an concerning it, and disputing about it and arguing about it by conjecture about the unseen."

Shaykh Muhammad al-Amin al-Shanqiti said in Adwa' al-Bayan (4/20): "Know that the story of the People of the Cave, their names, and in what place on earth they were—none of that has been authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) beyond what is in the Qur'an. The commentators have many Israelite reports on this, from which we have turned away because they are not trustworthy."

See also: al-Isra'iliyyat wa'l-Mawdu'at by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahba, pp. 235-237.]].

Zayd ibn Aslam said: The reason for Jibril's (peace be upon him) withholding from him was that there was a puppy in his house. When he came down, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rebuked him for his delay, and he said: "We do not enter a house in which there is a dog [or] [[In manuscript B: "wa la" (and not).]] an image." [[See hadiths on this: Musnad of Imam Ahmad: 1/148; al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib: 4/68-69.]]

They differed over the duration of the withholding of revelation from him. Ibn Jurayj said: twelve days. Ibn Abbas said: fifteen days. Muqatil said: forty days.

They said: The polytheists said: "Muhammad's Lord has left him and detested him." So Allah the Exalted revealed this surah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Jibril, you did not come until I longed for you." Jibril said: "I was more eager (for you), but I am a servant commanded (by my Lord)," and then (Allah) revealed: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾ [Maryam: 64]. [[Related by al-Tabari: 30/231, and Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir: 2/379, from Ma'mar. al-Suyuti added in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/541, attributing it to Ibn Mardawayh by way of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. See also: al-Fath al-Samawi: 3/1101.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿By the morning brightness﴾: He swore by the morning brightness and meant by it the whole day, as evidenced by His setting it against the night, saying: ﴿and by the night when it is still﴾. A parallel is His saying: ﴿Or are the people of the towns secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning brightness?﴾ [al-A'raf: 98], meaning: in the daytime.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: it means the time of the morning brightness (duha), which is the hour when the sun has risen and the day is moderate in heat and cold, in summer and in winter.

﴿And by the night when it is still﴾. al-Hasan said: it came with its darkness. This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. al-Walibi reported from him: "when it departs." Ata and al-Dahhak said: it covered everything with darkness. Mujahid said: it became level (istawa). Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: its darkness became calm and settled, so that it does not increase after that. It is said: "a still night (layl saj) and a still sea (bahr saj)" [when it is calm].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you.﴾ This is the answer to the oath, meaning: He has not left you since He chose you, nor has He hated you since He loved you.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 93, verses 5–6:

﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content.﴾ 'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: it is intercession for his community until he is content. This is also the view of 'Ali and al-Hasan.

We have also been related from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, my community, my community," and he wept. Then Allah said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say to him: We shall indeed content you regarding your community, and We shall not grieve you concerning them." [[Recorded by Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on the Prophet's (ﷺ) supplication and weeping out of compassion for them, no. (202): 1/191. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 15/165–166.]]

Harb ibn Shurayh said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali say: "You people of Iraq say: the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an is: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾. But we, the People of the House, say: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah is: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content﴾" [[Attributed by the author of al-Durr al-Manthur 8/543 to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah.]] — meaning of reward. And it was said: of victory, empowerment, and the multiplication of believers, ﴿so that you will be content﴾.

Then Allah, mighty and majestic, informed him of the state he was in before the revelation, and reminded him of His blessings, saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?﴾ Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani reported to me; Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Nisaburi informed us; Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us, and Abu 'Amr al-Juwayni and Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord for something, and I wished I had not asked for it. I said: O Lord, You gave Sulayman ibn Dawud a great kingdom, and You gave so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such? He said: O Muhammad, did I not find you an orphan and give you shelter? I said: Yes, O Lord. [He said: Did I not find you astray and guide you? I said: Yes, O Lord. He said: Did I not find you poor and make you rich? I said: Yes, O Lord.]" Another narrator, from Hammad, added: "Did I not open your chest and remove from you your burden? I said: Yes, O Lord." The meaning of the verse: Did He not find you an orphan, young and poor, when your parents died and left you neither wealth nor a shelter? So I made for you a shelter to which you could return, and I placed you under the care of your uncle Abu Talib, until he raised you well and relieved you of the burden.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 93, verses 5–6:

﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content.﴾ 'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: it is intercession for his community until he is content. This is also the view of 'Ali and al-Hasan.

We have also been related from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, my community, my community," and he wept. Then Allah said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say to him: We shall indeed content you regarding your community, and We shall not grieve you concerning them." [[Recorded by Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on the Prophet's (ﷺ) supplication and weeping out of compassion for them, no. (202): 1/191. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 15/165–166.]]

Harb ibn Shurayh said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali say: "You people of Iraq say: the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an is: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾. But we, the People of the House, say: the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah is: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be content﴾" [[Attributed by the author of al-Durr al-Manthur 8/543 to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah.]] — meaning of reward. And it was said: of victory, empowerment, and the multiplication of believers, ﴿so that you will be content﴾.

Then Allah, mighty and majestic, informed him of the state he was in before the revelation, and reminded him of His blessings, saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter?﴾ Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani reported to me; Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Nisaburi informed us; Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us, and Abu 'Amr al-Juwayni and Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord for something, and I wished I had not asked for it. I said: O Lord, You gave Sulayman ibn Dawud a great kingdom, and You gave so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such? He said: O Muhammad, did I not find you an orphan and give you shelter? I said: Yes, O Lord. [He said: Did I not find you astray and guide you? I said: Yes, O Lord. He said: Did I not find you poor and make you rich? I said: Yes, O Lord.]" Another narrator, from Hammad, added: "Did I not open your chest and remove from you your burden? I said: Yes, O Lord." The meaning of the verse: Did He not find you an orphan, young and poor, when your parents died and left you neither wealth nor a shelter? So I made for you a shelter to which you could return, and I placed you under the care of your uncle Abu Talib, until he raised you well and relieved you of the burden.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 93, verse 7–8:

﴿And He found you lost, and guided you﴾. That is, lost concerning what you were upon; ﴿and guided you﴾, meaning: He guided you to monotheism (tawhid) and prophethood.

Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: "And He found you lost" from the landmarks of prophethood and the rulings of the Sharia, unaware of them, and He guided you to them, [as He said] ﴿And indeed, you were before it among the unaware﴾ [Yusuf: 3], and He said: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was﴾ [al-Shura: 52].

It was also said: lost in the valleys (shi'ab) of Makkah, and He guided you back to your grandfather Abd al-Muttalib. Abu al-Duha narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got lost in the valleys of Makkah while he was a small child, and Abu Jahl saw him turning away from his sheep, and returned him to Abd al-Muttalib.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with his uncle Abu Talib in the caravan of Maysarah, the servant of Khadijah. One dark night, as he was riding his she-camel, Iblis came, seized the camel's halter and turned it away from the road. Then Gabriel came, and he blew a blast at Iblis, from which he fell to the land of Abyssinia, and he returned him to the caravan, and Allah bestowed His favour upon him by that. [[Ibn Kathir cited both reports in al-Tafsir (4/524) from al-Baghawi.]] It was also said: ﴿And He found you lost﴾ concerning yourself, not knowing who you were, so He made you know yourself and your state.

﴿And He found you poor, and enriched you﴾. That is, poor, and He made you rich through the wealth of Khadijah, then through the spoils of war.

Muqatil said: ﴿and satisfied you﴾ with what He gave you of provision. Al-Farra' chose this view and said: He was not rich in the abundance of wealth, but Allah made him content with what He gave him, and that is the true meaning of richness.

Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhamash al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, that he said: Abu Hurayrah informed us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Richness is not in having an abundance of goods, but true richness is richness of the soul."
[[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his recension of the Sahifah of Hammam ibn Munabbih, no. (62), p. 237, ed. Dr. Rif'at Fawzi. Also al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Riqaq, Bab al-Ghina ghina al-nafs: 11/271; Muslim, Kitab al-Zakat, Bab Laysa al-ghina 'an kathrat al-'arad, no. (1051): 2/726; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 14/243-244.]]

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Zaghartani [[In "A" (al-Zaghrghatati) and in "B" (al-Za'farani). The correct reading is what I have recorded.]] informed us; Ahmad ibn Sa'id informed us; Abu Yahya Muhammad ibn Abd Allah informed us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Shurahbil ibn Sharik narrated to me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Successful is the one who embraces Islam, is given sustenance sufficient for him, and Allah makes him content with what He has given him."
[[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Zakat, Bab fi al-Kafaf wa al-Qana'ah, no. (1054): 2/730; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/245.]]

Then He enjoined him concerning orphans and the poor, saying:

Then He enjoined him concerning orphans and the poor, saying:

**Qur'an 93:9: "So as for the orphan, do not oppress him."**

Mujahid said: "Do not belittle the orphan, for you too were an orphan." Al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: "Do not oppress him regarding his wealth, so that you take his rights because of his weakness."[[See: Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 3/274.]] The Arabs used to do this with orphans: they would take their wealth and wrong them in their rights.

Abu Bakr Muhammad Abdullah ibn Abi Tawba informed us; Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith informed us; Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i informed us; Abdullah[[In "A" it is "Abd," and the correct reading is what is given here.]] ibn Mahmud informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn al-Khallal informed us; Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Yahya[[Omitted in "B."]] ibn Sulayman, from Yazid ibn Abi Attab, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The best house among the Muslims is a house in which there is an orphan who is treated kindly, and the worst house among the Muslims is a house in which there is an orphan who is mistreated." Then he said, pointing with his two fingers: "I and the one who sponsors an orphan [in Paradise][[Omitted in "A."]] are like this," [and he pointed][[In "B": "and he was pointing."]] with his two fingers [the index finger (al-sabbabah) and the middle finger (al-wusta)][[Omitted in "A."]].[[A weak hadith, narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, p. 47; by Ibn Majah in al-Adab, chapter on the right of the orphan, no. 3679: 2/1213; by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): 6/337; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/43. Al-Bukhari said of him: "munkar al-hadith" (rejected in narration), and Abu Hatim said: "mudtarib al-hadith" (unstable in narration). Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the reliable narrators, and Ibn Khuzayma narrated his hadith in his Sahih, saying: "There is something in my soul about this hadith, for I do not know Yahya's reliability or unreliability; I only included his report because scholars differ about him." I say: what was clear to al-Bukhari and Abu Hatim was hidden from Ibn Khuzayma, so their criticism takes precedence over the one who deemed him reliable. See also: al-Iraqi and al-Zabidi's takhrij of the hadiths of Ihya' Ulum al-Din: 3/1209-1210; Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifa: 4/142.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 93, verses 10–11:**

﴿As for the one who asks, do not rebuke him.﴾ The exegetes (al-mufassirun) said: He means the one who asks at the door. The meaning is: do not rebuke him, do not drive him away when he asks you, for you were once poor. Either you feed him, or you turn him away gently. It is said: *nahara* and *intahara* (to rebuke, to scold) when one confronts a person with words that drive him off.

Qatadah said: Turn the one who asks away with mercy and gentleness. Ibrahim ibn Adham said: The askers are excellent people, for they carry our provision to the Hereafter.

Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i) said: The asker wants the Hereafter. He comes to the door of one of you and says: "Will you send something to your family?"

It is narrated from al-Hasan regarding His words, "As for the one who asks, do not rebuke him," that he said: "The seeker of knowledge."

﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it.﴾ Mujahid said: It means prophethood. Abu Bishr narrated this from him, and al-Zajjaj chose it and said: That is, convey what you have been sent with, and proclaim the prophethood which Allah has given you. [Allah] [[The word is missing from manuscript "A".]]

Al-Laith narrated from Mujahid: It means the Qur'an, and this is the view of al-Kalbi. He was commanded to recite it. [[In manuscript "B": "he recites it".]]

Muqatil said: Give thanks for the blessings mentioned in this surah that were bestowed upon you: the care for the orphan, guidance after going astray, and enrichment after poverty. And proclaiming the blessing of Allah is a form of thanks.

Abu Sa'id Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmi al-Bistami informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sakhtawayh told us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Nasr-abadi informed us, [Ali ibn Sa'id al-Nasawi told us] [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".]] Sa'id ibn Ufayr informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub told us, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Shurahbil, the client of the Ansar, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever is shown a kindness, let him repay it. If he cannot find anything to repay it with, let him praise the one who did it, for when he praises him, he has thanked him. And whoever conceals it has been ungrateful. And whoever adorns himself with what has not been given to him is like one who wears two garments of falsehood." [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, p. 69, from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Ufayr, from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Shurahbil, client of the Ansar, from Jabir. Shurahbil has been declared weak by more than one scholar, yet Ibn Hibban authenticated it (no. 2073, p. 506). It was also recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter "What has come concerning one who displays what he has not been given", through the chain of Isma'il ibn Abbas, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." It was also recorded by Abu Dawud in al-Adab, chapter "On thanking for a kindness" (7/179). The hadith has a supporting narration in Ahmad and al-Tabarani's al-Awsat. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/181): "It contains Salih ibn Abi al-Akhdar, who was declared trustworthy despite his weakness, and the rest of Ahmad's narrators are trustworthy; so it is a sound hadith through its chains."]]

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn Mani' told us, saying: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, that is al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say from the pulpit: "Whoever does not thank for little does not thank for much. And whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah, the Exalted. Proclaiming the blessing of Allah is thanks, and abandoning it is disbelief. Community is mercy, and division is punishment." [[Recorded by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/278), and by his son Abd Allah in the Zawa'id of al-Musnad (4/375). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/218): "It was narrated by Abd Allah ibn Ahmad, al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani, and their narrators are trustworthy." Al-Ajluni said in Kashf al-Khafa' (2/336): "Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Istina' al-Ma'ruf from al-Nu'man, and Abd Allah ibn Ahmad recorded it with a chain that is acceptable..." Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/545) to al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab with a weak chain. Ibn Kathir declared it weak (4/524). See also al-Albani, Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah (2/276–277).]]

The Sunnah, in the recitation of the people of Makkah, is that one says the takbir (Allahu akbar) from the beginning of the surah "al-Duha" at the start of each surah, until one finishes the Qur'an.

The Imam, the most eminent shaykh, Muhyi al-Sunnah, Nasir al-Hadith, the model of the imams, Nashir al-Din, Rukn al-Islam, Imam of the imams, Mufti of the East, Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Mas'ud, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I recited it thus to the reciter-imam Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Hamidi in Marw, who said: I read to Abu al-Qasim Tahir ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, who said: I read to Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Mihran, who said: I read to Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamid al-Saffar the reciter, who said: I read to Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hashimi, who said: I read to Abu Rabi'ah and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Haddad, and both of them recited to Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi Bazzah, and Ibn Abi Bazzah [Ibn Abi Bazzah] [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "B".]] informed them that he had recited to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman ibn Kathir al-Makki, and Ikrimah informed him that he had recited to Shibl ibn Abbad and Isma'il ibn Qustantin, and both of them informed him that they had recited to Abd Allah ibn Kathir, and Abd Allah [ibn Kathir, may Allah be pleased with them all] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] informed them that he had recited to Mujahid, and Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

Imam Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali also informed us, and I read to him in Marw; he said: Al-Sharif Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Muhammad al-Zaydi informed me of the takbir, and I read to him in the frontier town of Harran, who said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Mawsili, known as al-Naqqash, told us, and I read to him in the city of Salam (Baghdad), who said: Abu Rabi'ah Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Rab'i told us, and I read to him in Makkah, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi [Bazzah] [[In manuscript "A" it reads "Tawbah"; the correct reading is what is given here.]] told us, and I read to him. He said to me: I recited it to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman, and he informed me that he had recited to Isma'il ibn Qustantin and Shibl ibn Abbad. He said: When I reached "al-Duha," they both said to me: "Say the takbir until you finish, with the end of every surah, for we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us to do that, and he informed us that he had recited to Mujahid and Mujahid commanded him to do that, and Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, and he commanded him to do that, and Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and he commanded him to do that, and Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Prophet ﷺ, and he commanded him to do that." [[Ibn Kathir cited it (4/522) and then said: "This is a Sunnah uniquely transmitted by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Bazzi, from the descendants of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, and he was an imam in the readings. As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi declared him weak and said: 'I do not narrate from him,' and likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said he was munkar al-hadith. But Shaykh Shihab al-Din Abu Shamah related in his commentary on al-Shatibiyyah, from al-Shafi'i, that he heard a man recite this takbir in prayer, and said: 'You have done well and correctly followed the Sunnah,' and this implies the soundness of this report." See on this matter al-Nawawi's al-Tibyan fi Adab Hamalat al-Qur'an.]]

The reason for the takbir was that when the revelation was delayed, the polytheists said: "His Shaytan has forsaken him and bid him farewell." The Prophet ﷺ was saddened by this. When "al-Duha" was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbir out of joy at the descent of the revelation, and so they made it a Sunnah. [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir (4/522), who said: "It has not been narrated with a chain by which it can be judged sound or weak, and Allah knows best."]]

If he cannot find anything to repay it with, let him praise the one who did it, for when he praises him, he has thanked him. And whoever conceals it has been ungrateful. And whoever adorns himself with what has not been given to him is like one who wears two garments of falsehood." [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, p. 69, from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Ufayr, from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Shurahbil, client of the Ansar, from Jabir. Shurahbil has been declared weak by more than one scholar, yet Ibn Hibban authenticated it (no. 2073, p. 506). It was also recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter "What has come concerning one who displays what he has not been given", through the chain of Isma'il ibn Abbas, from Umarah ibn Ghaziyyah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." It was also recorded by Abu Dawud in al-Adab, chapter "On thanking for a kindness" (7/179). The hadith has a supporting narration in Ahmad and al-Tabarani's al-Awsat. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/181): "It contains Salih ibn Abi al-Akhdar, who was declared trustworthy despite his weakness, and the rest of Ahmad's narrators are trustworthy; so it is a sound hadith through its chains."]]

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn Mani' told us, saying: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, that is al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say from the pulpit: "Whoever does not thank for little does not thank for much. And whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah, the Exalted. Proclaiming the blessing of Allah is thanks, and abandoning it is disbelief. Community is mercy, and division is punishment." [[Recorded by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/278), and by his son Abd Allah in the Zawa'id of al-Musnad (4/375). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/218): "It was narrated by Abd Allah ibn Ahmad, al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani, and their narrators are trustworthy." Al-Ajluni said in Kashf al-Khafa' (2/336): "Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Istina' al-Ma'ruf from al-Nu'man, and Abd Allah ibn Ahmad recorded it with a chain that is acceptable..." Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/545) to al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab with a weak chain. Ibn Kathir declared it weak (4/524). See also al-Albani, Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah (2/276–277).]]

The Sunnah, in the recitation of the people of Makkah, is that one says the takbir (Allahu akbar) from the beginning of the surah "al-Duha" at the start of each surah, until one finishes the Qur'an.

The Imam, the most eminent shaykh, Muhyi al-Sunnah, Nasir al-Hadith, the model of the imams, Nashir al-Din, Rukn al-Islam, Imam of the imams, Mufti of the East, Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Mas'ud, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I recited it thus to the reciter-imam Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Hamidi in Marw, who said: I read to Abu al-Qasim Tahir ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, who said: I read to Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Mihran, who said: I read to Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamid al-Saffar the reciter, who said: I read to Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hashimi, who said: I read to Abu Rabi'ah and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Haddad, and both of them recited to Abu al-Husayn ibn Abi Bazzah, and Ibn Abi Bazzah [Ibn Abi Bazzah] [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "B".]] informed them that he had recited to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman ibn Kathir al-Makki, and Ikrimah informed him that he had recited to Shibl ibn Abbad and Isma'il ibn Qustantin, and both of them informed him that they had recited to Abd Allah ibn Kathir, and Abd Allah [ibn Kathir, may Allah be pleased with them all] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] informed them that he had recited to Mujahid, and Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.

Imam Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali also informed us, and I read to him in Marw; he said: Al-Sharif Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Muhammad al-Zaydi informed me of the takbir, and I read to him in the frontier town of Harran, who said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Mawsili, known as al-Naqqash, told us, and I read to him in the city of Salam (Baghdad), who said: Abu Rabi'ah Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Rab'i told us, and I read to him in Makkah, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi [Bazzah] [[In manuscript "A" it reads "Tawbah"; the correct reading is what is given here.]] told us, and I read to him. He said to me: I recited it to Ikrimah ibn Sulayman, and he informed me that he had recited to Isma'il ibn Qustantin and Shibl ibn Abbad. He said: When I reached "al-Duha," they both said to me: "Say the takbir until you finish, with the end of every surah, for we recited to Ibn Kathir and he commanded us to do that, and he informed us that he had recited to Mujahid and Mujahid commanded him to do that, and Mujahid informed him that he had recited to Ibn Abbas, and he commanded him to do that, and Ibn Abbas informed him that he had recited to Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and he commanded him to do that, and Ubayy informed him that he had recited to the Prophet ﷺ, and he commanded him to do that." [[Ibn Kathir cited it (4/522) and then said: "This is a Sunnah uniquely transmitted by Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Bazzi, from the descendants of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, and he was an imam in the readings. As for hadith, Abu Hatim al-Razi declared him weak and said: 'I do not narrate from him,' and likewise Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said he was munkar al-hadith. But Shaykh Shihab al-Din Abu Shamah related in his commentary on al-Shatibiyyah, from al-Shafi'i, that he heard a man recite this takbir in prayer, and said: 'You have done well and correctly followed the Sunnah,' and this implies the soundness of this report." See on this matter al-Nawawi's al-Tibyan fi Adab Hamalat al-Qur'an.]]

The reason for the takbir was that when the revelation was delayed, the polytheists said: "His Shaytan has forsaken him and bid him farewell." The Prophet ﷺ was saddened by this. When "al-Duha" was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the takbir out of joy at the descent of the revelation, and so they made it a Sunnah. [[Mentioned by Ibn Kathir (4/522), who said: "It has not been narrated with a chain by which it can be judged sound or weak, and Allah knows best."]]
